value: Study cohort: 41 healthy controls, 56 pre-hypertensive subjects, 99 hypertensive patients (n=196 total)
All participants from Kailuan Group Corporation cohort study in Tangshan, northern China
Shotgun metagenomic sequencing: 1211 Gb 125-bp paired-end reads, average 6.18 ± 1.43 million reads per sample
Blood pressure classification: controls SBP ≤125 mmHg or DBP ≤80 mmHg; pHTN 125 < SBP ≤ 139 or 80 < DBP ≤ 89; HTN SBP ≥140 or DBP ≥90
Exclusion criteria: cancer, heart failure, renal failure, smoking, stroke, peripheral artery disease, chronic inflammatory disease
No antibiotics or probiotics within 8 weeks prior to enrollment
Metabolomic analysis subset: 30 controls, 31 pHTN, 63 HTN (n=124)
Fecal microbiota transplantation: GF mice (n=5 control, n=10 HTN) inoculated with human fecal contents from 1 control and 2 HTN donors
BP measured by tail-cuff method at 10 weeks post-transplantation in mice
HTN mice showed significantly higher SBP, DBP, MBP compared to control mice (P < 0.05)

extraction_warnings: Sample-level data was not individually reported in the paper. Samples represent generic placeholders based on the three reported study groups (41 healthy controls, 56 pre-hypertensives, 99 hypertensives; total n=196). Individual participant identifiers and per-sample metadata are not available in the provided text.

Age, sex, and other demographic characteristics were reported at the group level (in Table S1, referenced but not fully shown in the provided text) rather than per-sample. The paper states 'Other than SBP and DBP, there was no significant difference in other clinical parameters among groups'.
The paper reports metagenomic data from 196 samples but does not provide individual sample-level identifiers or detailed per-sample metadata beyond group assignments.
Metabolomic analysis was performed on a subset of 124 subjects (30 healthy controls, 31 pHTNs, 63 HTNs), not the full cohort, but individual sample identifiers were not provided.
Batch 1 returned granularity='subgroup_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.
Batch 1 subgroups ['Healthy controls', 'Pre-hypertension', 'Hypertension', 'HTN mice (recipient after procedure)', 'Control mice (recipient after procedure)'] differ from batch 0 []; kept batch 0.
Human participants' age in years not reported in the provided text; demographic table (Table S1) referenced but not included.
BMI values mentioned in correlation analysis but specific numbers not provided in main text.
Gender distribution noted as discrepant among groups (Table S1) but specific proportions not provided in excerpted sections.
Fecal microbiota transplantation involved only 3 human donors (2 HTN, 1 control) and 16 recipient mice total; limited donor sample size acknowledged by authors.
Mice cohort includes both males and females implied for germ-free mice housing, but sex not explicitly stated for all recipient mice groups.
Blood pressure measurements on mice performed by tail-cuff method within 60 min of removal from germ-free isolators; potential contamination risk noted by authors.
Batch 2 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.

Schema fields 'disease_response_os', 'disease_response_os_unit', 'ecog_performance_status', 'tumor_size_measurement', and 'tumor_size_residual_measurement' are not applicable to this hypertension/microbiota study. These are oncology-focused metrics. No values extracted for these fields.
The paper is a cross-sectional observational study with no survival follow-up or tumor endpoints. Biomarker values are relative abundances and metabolite levels, not absolute measurements.
Fecal microbiota transplantation study involved only 3 human donors (1 control, 2 HTN) and small numbers of recipient mice (n=5 control, n=10 HTN), limiting generalizability.

Multiple subgroups (control, pHTN, HTN) are analyzed throughout but granularity set to study_level because the schema does not request subgroup-stratified extraction. Subgroup comparisons are available in the source material.
